description: Single-panel binary Fe-Al equilibrium phase diagram (redrawn from ref. 14). Temperature (°C) is on the left axis (200-1600); Al content is plotted twice, as at.% on the bottom axis (0-100, ticks every 10) and as wt.% on the top axis (0-100). The large upper region is labelled L (liquid), bounded by liquidus lines descending from 1530 °C at pure Fe through annotated points at 1310 °C, 1215 °C, 1164 °C and 1171 °C toward 660 °C at pure Al (99.1). Fe-rich side: α-Fe (bcc) field with 1394 °C, a narrow γ-Fe austenite field (1195 °C) closing at 912 °C, a 770 °C magnetic-transformation line, the ordered Fe3Al (D03) field with an α + D03 two-phase region, the FeAl (B2) field with an α + B2 region below ~1092 °C, plus a 1157 °C invariant. The Al-rich side labels Fe2Al5, FeAl2 and FeAl3 between roughly 50 and 75 at.% Al, with a (Al) solid-solution region bounded near 652 °C/660 °C. The figure shows how far Al dissolves in bcc Fe before brittle B2/D03 intermetallics appear.

observations.observation: The figure is a binary Fe-Al phase diagram with temperature (°C) from 200 to 1600 on the ordinate and Al content given twice: at.% on the lower abscissa and wt.% on the upper abscissa, both running 0-100.
The uppermost region of the diagram is labelled 'L' (liquid), bounded by liquidus curves that fall from 1530 °C at the pure-Fe corner to 660 °C at the pure-Al corner.
Annotated temperatures printed on the diagram include 1530 °C, 1394 °C, 1195 °C, 1310 °C, 1215 °C, 1164 °C, 1171 °C, 1157 °C, 1092 °C, 912 °C, 770 °C, 652 °C and 660 °C.
The Fe-rich side shows the α-Fe field, a narrow γ-Fe austenite field (1394 °C / 1195 °C labels) that closes at 912 °C, and a dashed 'Magnetic transformation' line near 770 °C.
Ordered phases are labelled in the central part of the diagram as FeAl (B2) and Fe3Al (D03), together with two-phase fields marked 'α + B2' and 'α + D03'.
On the Al-rich side the intermetallic phases Fe2Al5, FeAl2 and FeAl3 are labelled between roughly 50 and 75 at.% Al, and a terminal '(Al)' solid-solution region is bounded near 652 °C/660 °C.
The caption identifies the figure as the Fe-Al phase diagram (ref. 14).
The citing text states that Al forms a disordered solid solution in Fe up to about 11 wt.% of alloying.
The citing text states that beyond about 11 wt.% Al, intermetallic phases such as D03-based Fe3Al and B2-based FeAl appear, and that these intermetallics are usually brittle.
The citing text measures density of Al = 2.7 g cm-3 and of Si = 2.3 g cm-3 as the motivation for using Al (and sometimes Si) as the chief alloying element in low-density bulk steels.
The label '99.1' is printed near the pure-Al corner next to 660 °C; its exact meaning is not self-evident from the diagram alone.

subfigures.description: Complete binary Fe-Al phase diagram with dual Al axis (at.% bottom, wt.% top) and temperature (°C) on the left; labelled phase fields L, α-Fe, γ-Fe, FeAl (B2), Fe3Al (D03), Fe2Al5, FeAl2, FeAl3, (Al), plus α + B2, α + D03, a magnetic-transformation line and numerous annotated thermal-arrest temperatures.
